useful_references.complete_statement: Solution 1 encodes the unoccupied squares as a monotone path from (1,n) to (m,1); a legal move changes an ES corner to SE, and reversing SE corners reaches every path.
expanded_definitions: E increases the first coordinate by one; S decreases the second coordinate by one.
The path is represented by its m+n-1 occupied vertices/unoccupied board squares.
applicability_check: The initial holes are exactly the top row union right column, the vertices of E^(m-1)S^(n-1).
The three holes required by a legal move are exactly the vertices of a local ES corner.
proof_insights: Use inversion number of the E/S word to justify termination of reverse SE-to-ES switches.
